issues.failure_explanation: For |a|<\mu the point x=a lies in the quadratic branch, so \phi_\mu(a)=a^2/\mu^2, not 1. The displayed evaluation is therefore false for a subcase of |a|<\sqrt{\mu^2+2\lambda}; the strict inequality at a=0 also fails. The theorem's conclusion is not established by the proof as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the case analysis by treating x=a as a candidate only when |a|>\mu and handle the tie a=0 without requiring strict inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the scalar proximal map result is unreliable, although the statement itself appears true.
issues.title: False intermediate evaluation in proximal proof
issues.why_classification: A local proof repair fixes the defective step and preserves the theorem's conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: If \cI_1\cup\cI_2 is empty, the minimum over an empty set is undefined. The existence of a unit null vector with \vv_i\neq0 for all i in \cI_0 is asserted but not derived from the stated rank hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the empty-set case (e.g., set rho to any positive number) and justify the null-vector choice by excluding a finite union of proper subspaces of the nullspace.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the noise-free differentiability-at-optimizer result has a degenerate-case gap.
issues.title: Undefined rho and unproved null-vector construction in differentiability proof
issues.why_classification: These are local completion steps that do not change the theorem's conclusion or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that $\mathrm{spark}(A)=m+1$ and the initial value $\cQ_\mu(\wvx^0,\widehat\vomega^0)< \mathrm{spark}(A)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The inequality (n-m)>m requires n>2m, which is not a formal hypothesis in the BCD derivation or Theorem covgergalg1. If |\cI_2^j|<m, then A_{\cI_2^j}A_{\cI_2^j}^\top need not be invertible, so the displayed x-update is undefined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit dimensional condition such as n>2m (or card(I_2^j)>=m with full row rank) to the noise-free update and convergence theorem, or provide a separate case for card(I_2^j)<m.
issues.overall_effect: The noise-free BCD scheme and its convergence statement are not well-defined under only spark(A)=m+1 and Q_0<spark(A).
issues.title: Noise-free BCD update assumes an unproved cardinality inequality
issues.why_classification: The paper already operates in the m<<n regime; adding the missing local dimension condition preserves the intended guarantee without new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: if and only if $\abs{\wvx_i}\neq \mu$ for all $i$
According to Theorem \ref{noise_optcond}, the limit point $(\wvx,\widehat{\vomega})$ is a minimizer of model \eqref{obj_singleu}.

issues.failure_explanation: The limit point may satisfy |\wvx_i|=\mu; H_\mu then sets omega_i=0, and the BCD fixed point need not be a local minimizer. The proofs invoke linearoptcond/noise_optcond, whose hypotheses include |\wvx_i|\neq\mu, without establishing it. Concrete noise-free counterexample: A=[1,1/2], b=5/4, mu=1, x0=(1,1/2), omega0=(0,0) gives Q=5/4<spark(A)=2 and is a fixed BCD point, but (eps,-2eps) feasible perturbations lower Phi for small eps>0. Concrete noisy counterexample: A=[1,1/2], b=23/12, alpha=3, mu=1, same x0, omega0 gives J=23/12<2 and is fixed, while increasing x_1 lowers G.

failure_location.quote: Theorem  \ref{linearoptcond} establishes that $(\wvx, \widehat{\vomega})$ is a minimizer of the model \eqref{constrain_model}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must alter the BCD tie-breaking/update or prove that all BCD limit points satisfy |x_i|\neq mu, and then re-establish finite convergence to a minimizer.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised finite-step convergence guarantees of Algorithm BCD for the noise-free and noisy models are false as stated; the algorithm may stop at a non-minimizer.
issues.title: BCD finite-convergence theorems can converge to non-minimizers with |x_i|=mu
issues.why_classification: A counterexample under the stated hypotheses invalidates a central convergence guarantee; no local correction preserves the advertised claim without a new argument or algorithm change.

issues.failure_explanation: The denominator m-n+card(K+1) can be nonpositive. Since m<n and K+1 is an arbitrary index set of small entries, the square root may be undefined (negative radicand) or divide by zero. The cited lemmas do not imply card(K+1)>n-m.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the update only when m-n+card(K+1)>0 and supply a valid fallback (or a new formula), with an argument that the resulting mu_{k+1} preserves the required invertibility/stability, or replace the formula by a valid continuation schedule.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm continuescheme is not a well-defined procedure as written, and the claimed stabilization by the continuation update is unsupported.
issues.title: Mu-continuation update formula is undefined for admissible sets
issues.why_classification: The defect is confined to one heuristic update rule, but a complete repair needs a new contained argument/construction; it does not collapse the main BCD theorems.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A higher SNR corresponds to a lower noise level.
